message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Finals MVP awards. His accolades include four regular‑season MVP awards, 19 All‑NBA selections, 18 All‑Defensive Team selections, and 17 NBA All‑Star appearances.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy—most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron to support at‑risk youth. He is also a media entrepreneur, co‑founding the entertainment company SpringHill Entertainment and producing films and television series. In addition, he has been active in social justice causes, using his platform to advocate for civil rights and community empowerment.
